text:
maya: Ran an offline replay (prod-trace-2026-03-10) with the new 'token-siphon' continuous-batching heuristic. Quick dump of findings below, pls skim and react.
liam: thanks — is that the run with kernel-prefer=auto?
sophia: yep, auto+kv-prefetch=on? curious about warmup behavior.
maya: correct. TL;DR: overall throughput up ~3%, avg latency flat, but p95/p99 regressed for short sequences (~<32 tokens) when a kernel switch happens mid-batch. suspect kv-cache warmup + kernel handoff.
kevin: can you paste the sim config you used?
maya: sure:
```
SIM_CONFIG={
  replay_trace: "prod-trace-2026-03-10",
  heuristic: "token-siphon-v2",
  kernel_preference: "auto",
  token_budget_target: 1024,
  kv_prefetch: true,
  batch_timeout_ms: 8,
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
}
```
perf-bot: sim-job #4521 finished. summary: p50=22ms, p90=115ms, p95=260ms (+18% vs baseline), p99=980ms (+40% vs baseline), cost_per_1k_tokens=-2.7%.
tara: ugh p99 jump is worrying. where are the faults concentrated?
maya: filtered by sequence length: short seqs (<32) p95 from 120->210ms. Long seqs stable or slightly better. Kernel-switch events correlate. I attached a small trace snippet:
```
# trace 0xabc: seq_len=24, batch formed with 6 items, kernelA->kernelB at token 12, kv-miss on request 3, latency spiked to 480ms
# trace 0xdef: seq_len=16, batch 4 items, no kernel switch, p95 ~90ms
```
liam: hypothesis: kernel selector is prioritizing cheaper kernel for leading tokens but when a long item appears it forces a switch, which flushes kernels and causes KV cold path. maybe our KV warming only primed for the first kernel.
sophia: we also saw a similar pattern in the profiling logs: many small memcpy+scheduler stalls during handoff. attaching perf counters in-thread:
```
COUNTERS: kernel_switches=312, kv_prefetch_hits=1.1k, kv_prefetch_misses=420, memcpy_ms_total=85, scheduler_stalls=37ms
```
kevin: two actionable levers: 1) add hysteresis to kernel selection (avoid switch if switch cost > estimated benefit), 2) prioritize KV prefetch for potential downstream kernels when batch contains heterogeneous sequence lengths.
tara: + add a metric in console: kernel_handoff_count per route + median fallout latency post-handoff. We need this for the A/B.
maya: agree. Proposal: run A/B eval harness on 10k traces: A=token-siphon-v2 (current), B=token-siphon-v2+hysteresis+proactive-kv. 50/50 split, measure p95/p99 by seq_len buckets.
liam: also include a micro-experiment disabling kernel auto-swap (force single kernel per batch) to measure max handoff cost.
perf-bot: scheduled a/b job #4522 with splits. ETA ~2h. will post full CSV.
sophia: for the offline replay tool, add an event for 'kernel_switch_reason' and 'kv_warm_state' so we can filter traces automatically.
kevin: i'll push a small patch to the selector: add candidate_score -= handoff_penalty if predicted_switch && batch_time_left < threshold. keeping patch tiny.
maya: thanks. sam (ops) FYI this might touch dedicated pools routing but should be safe behind sim. @tara i'll need you to wire the new console metrics.
tara: on it. will add dashboard w/ per-route kernel_handoff_count and a waterfall for post-handoff latencies. ETA EOD.
liam: good plan. if A/B shows the hysteresis helps we can quantify cost tradeoff (cost_per_tok vs p99).
maya: final note: keep token_budget_target=1024 for experiments. If we lower it the batch formation changes and may mask the handoff.
sophia: copied. will also run a focused run with token_budget_target=512 to observe sensitivity.
maya: thanks all — will post the perf CSV and a short summary once perf-bot completes. :mag: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
